# M4 OperandList draft

This directory is an isolated working copy. The parent patch is `/tmp/perf-m4-operand-list.patch`; it is not applied to the repository. The isolated test source was formatted with clang-format 19 and compiled/run using the Makefile-probed g++ C++2c mode in both native `inplace_vector` selection and forced fallback mode; each run passed 5/5 tests. Source remains frozen.

## Patch scope

- Add `vortex/operand_list.hpp`: eight inline `gleditor::cpp26::inplace_vector` cells, vector spill from append nine, `span`, data/iterator/index/front/back/size/empty/clear, no vector conversion, explicit copy/move and moved-from reset. `BasicOperandList<Allocator>` is deliberately fixed to `CellRef`; a stateless allocator parameter exists only to test spill-allocation failure. Production uses `OperandList = BasicOperandList<>`.
- Change `VortexCore::{wingOf,inputsOf,outputsOf}` and `VortexVM::{inputsOf,outputsOf}` signatures; build the core result by rank-order append, preserve operand/master resolution and VM runtime-slot rewriting.
- Migrate every direct vector assignment from these wing APIs found by repository-wide search: VM dispatch, frames, stdlib, VQL/VPL compiler, and the existing core test. The VM's `resolveCell` read-only boundary becomes `span<const CellRef>`, accepting either the new contiguous list or existing vectors without ownership conversion.
- Add new xuzz tests for arities 0/8/9/1024, order and mutable span, inline/spill copy/move/move-from reuse, injected ninth-element allocation failure preserving all eight old items, spilled copy-assignment allocation failure preserving an inline destination with successful retry, no implicit vector conversion, expected 64-byte ABI, and a VortexCore end-to-end 0/8/9/128 wing test.
- Does not edit `getOpcodeKind` or classification precedence.

## Layout reasoning, not measured

For the pinned Beman fallback, `inplace_vector<uint32_t,8>` is expected to contain 32 bytes of inline elements plus a one-byte size field rounded to 36 bytes at 4-byte alignment. `std::vector<CellRef>` is expected to occupy 24 bytes on the host ABI. The combined 60-byte members round to 64 bytes at the class's 8-byte alignment. This is only an ABI-layout calculation; the draft test asserts the plan target and should be observed on the actual supported Clang/library configuration. Native `std::inplace_vector` must be checked too.

## Verification status

After formatting the isolated copies with clang-format 19, syntax-only checks passed for `vortex_core.cpp`, `vortex_vm.cpp`, `vortex_frames.cpp`, `vortex_stdlib.cpp`, `vql/compiler.cpp`, `vpl/compiler.cpp`, `operand_list_test.cpp`, and `vortex_core_test.cpp` using `/usr/bin/clang++`, the Make control `-std=c++2c` flags, and the draft Vortex include overlay before root fallbacks. No consumer object was linked, and no repository engine objects or full project build were used. The existing standalone helper binaries from the earlier g++ native/fallback runs still report 5/5 each; this verification window ended before rerunning the latest helper in normal/ASan/UBSan modes.

## Review required before use

Check cross-library layout and fallback/native move traits against other supported toolchains, all direct and indirect vector-boundary calls, and `std::span`'s converting range constructor for this iterator/data surface. The allocator parameter is constrained to an empty, nothrow-copyable allocator so move/copy never depend on unequal stateful allocators. It exists only to test spill-allocation failure without global allocation interposition.

# M4 capacity and access alternatives

This is an isolated experiment under `/tmp`; it changes neither the M4 source patch nor the repository. `operand_representation_probe.cpp` compares an existing vector-return pattern with inline-4 and inline-8 versions of the isolated draft, a caller-owned span buffer (8-cell stack array with unbounded vector spill), and a stateless visitor. The experiment-only header parameterizes inline capacity and adds a capacity accessor; production API/policy remain unchanged.

Run `experiment/operand_representation_probe` for layout/allocation rows. It is diagnostic-only and uses a counting allocator; it has no timing mode. Run `experiment/operand_timing_primary` for primary timings (optionally `--iterations N`). The primary executable uses only default `std::allocator`, contains no replacement global allocation operators, and does no allocation counting. It has separate phases for build/return/fill/mutable runtime-slot-like rewrite/checksum/destruction, copy plus mutation/checksum, and move plus mutation/checksum/destruction. Copy/move source setup is outside each phase timer. The timing binary was compiled but not run while PGO build activity was ongoing.

The probe uses identical values and rewrite/checksum logic for each representation and cohorts 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 64, and 1024. These cohorts are deliberately unweighted. They do not infer application weights from the curated synthetic M0 0/8/9 histogram. Real M0 arity and allocation data should weight the later paired timings.

`results/layout-allocation.csv` was produced with the Make-generated C++2c compiler configuration and optimized flags, with no engine objects linked. All five layouts produced identical checksums in all eight cohorts. The diagnostic allocator counts requested element bytes and overlapping old/new vector buffers; it excludes allocator metadata and does not report RSS. The primary timing executable has no allocation instrumentation.

## Observed host layout and allocation data

- `std::vector<CellRef>` object: 24 bytes. Inline-4: 48 bytes. Inline-8: 64 bytes. Caller span scratch owner (8-cell array plus spill vector): 56 bytes; the returned `std::span<CellRef>` itself is 16 bytes on this host. Visitor owns no operand object.
- Arity 0/1/2/4: inline-4 and inline-8, caller span, and visitor made no operand allocations. Vector allocated 0/1/2/3 times for 0/1/2/4 respectively.
- Arity 8: inline-8 and caller span allocated nothing. Inline-4 spilled and made two allocations (60 requested bytes total, 40 live, 60 peak); vector made four allocations (60 requested, 32 live, 48 peak).
- Arity 9: inline-8 and caller span each made one 36-byte allocation. Inline-4 made two allocations (60 total, 40 live, 60 peak); vector made five (124 total, 64 live, 96 peak).
- Arity 64: vector 7 allocations / 508 requested bytes / 384-byte peak; inline-4 5 / 620 / 480; inline-8 4 / 540 / 432; caller span 1 / 256 / 256; visitor 0.
- Arity 1024: vector 11 / 8,188 requested bytes / 6,144 peak; inline-4 9 / 10,220 / 7,680; inline-8 8 / 9,180 / 6,912; caller span 1 / 4,096 / 4,096; visitor 0.
- Copying a spilled vector or operand list made one allocation; moving it made none. Inline copies at or below their threshold made no allocation. The output's copy/move table records this separately from result construction.

Visitor passes values directly to the callback. It has no mutable contiguous result for consumers that rewrite runtime slots and then inspect or reuse the operand list. Caller-owned span retains mutable contiguous access but moves ownership/lifetime to the caller and needs a spill vector above eight; the probe uses known arity to reserve the exact spill size. These API differences must be accounted for in consumer integration and later end-to-end measurements.

# Isolated M5a VM table-alias overlay

This overlay tests changing VortexVM's ten private table aliases to the current
ReversibleCellMap/Set facade while leaving the production ChoicePoint snapshot
rollback algorithm and existing local snapshot/copy-swap transactions intact.
It adds no VM trail, savepoint, first-write tracking, root-steal rebase, or new
undo semantics. Nothing in this directory is wired into the checkout.

## Overlay files

- `apps/common/xanadu/vortex/vortex_vm.hpp`: aliases and private member types
  for cell references, streams, iterators, stream/iterator memberships,
  activation frames, guard stacks, pending checks, guard scopes, and mutation
  groups. ChoicePoint copies use the same facade type. RuntimeBindingSnapshot
  stays an ordinary unordered_map DTO.
- `apps/common/xanadu/vortex/reversible_cell_map.hpp`: copied standalone
  container facade. Default aliases use the default PMR resource (backed by
  new/delete); per-map custom resources exist only in helper fault tests.
- `vortex_vm.cpp`: lookup helper `resolveCell` accepts the migrated map;
  `pruneAssemblyState` uses facade-local `eraseIf` / `eraseIfKey`, not a
  `std::erase_if` overload. Prune semantics remain physical/irreversible here,
  matching the snapshot-only experiment.
- `vortex_bindings.cpp`: staged restore maps/sets use the facade; the external
  binding snapshot DTO remains standard maps. Typed set range walks use
  `forEachKey`, since the facade set wraps map storage.
- `vortex_comparison.cpp`: read-only comparison operand helper accepts the
  facade's private typed sets.

## Snapshot semantics preserved in this experiment

ChoicePoint copies still make independent copies of all live map/set state and
keep their current swap-back behavior. With no trail enabled, convenience
erase/clear/prune physically remove entries, so snapshots contain no retained
absent buckets. Value semantics match the old tables: optional values copy;
shared_ptr payloads share ownership; ActivationStack copies its shared_ptr
handles. RuntimeBindingSnapshot's cell reference/stream/iterator DTOs remain
`std::unordered_map` to preserve descriptor and caller-facing representation.

The facade hash changes physical iteration order (SplitMix64 avalanche instead
of identity hashing). Existing unordered iteration order was not a contract;
all serializer, binding, choice, restore, and comparison results still need
focused engine correctness checks before alias integration.

## Iterator/reference audit for current call sites

- `CopyCellRefs` snapshots all source scalar/stream/iterator handles into local
  records before writing any target. The local `shared_ptr` values survive map
  rehash and prevent alias writes from invalidating source data.
- Stream accumulation reads/copies the existing shared handle into a local
  before COW/append and before assigning the target entry.
- Iterator-next paths hold a local `shared_ptr<IteratorState>` before COW and
  replace the map entry before subsequent operations. No map iterator is kept
  across same-map insert/erase.
- `activationFrames_.at(cursor)` returns a reference used immediately to pop
  the top frame. On final close, that reference is not used after erasing the
  owner key. On nonfinal pop, the key is not erased.
- `vortex_bindings.cpp` range scans of cell references are read-only. Typed-set
  scans now call `forEachKey`; each callback inspects the separate payload map
  and mutates only the binding DTO. No source loop modifies the table it walks.
- `pruneAssemblyState` predicates inspect the current key and ArenaManifold
  membership; they do not retain `it->second` or a key reference after erasure.
  The facade's indexed iterator erase computes the next index before removing
  the current entry and does not rehash during deletion.
- Choice, binding-restore, frame, guard, and mutation-group map copy/swap paths
  operate on whole tables. The current code does not retain an element
  reference/iterator across those swaps. The table members are private, with no
  public getters exposing references.

Unlike `std::unordered_map`, a facade growth moves entries and invalidates
references as well as iterators; facade swap invalidates its owner/index
iterators rather than making them follow elements. The audit above is a
call-site reading, not a guarantee for future code. Keep it as an explicit
review gate. Snapshot creation and any use that spans a write must copy mapped
optional/shared_ptr handles into local values first.

## Syntax validation

The overlay was selected ahead of `apps/` in the repo compiler flags from
`make perf-print-flags`. `clang++ -fsyntax-only` passed these ten Vortex TUs:

- `vortex_resume.cpp`, `vortex_frames.cpp`, `vortex_closures.cpp`,
  `vortex_bindings.cpp`, `logic_relations.cpp`, `vortex_vm.cpp`,
  `vortex_contracts.cpp`, `vortex_string.cpp`, `vortex_streams.cpp`, and
  `vortex_comparison.cpp`.

The first attempt found actual compatibility gaps: `resolveCell` accepted only
`std::unordered_map`, `ChoiceSnapshotView` spelled its set/frame-map types
concretely, bindings staged restore used raw standard sets, and the binding
snapshot DTO shared the alias that was being migrated. Those are fixed in the
overlay; the DTO deliberately retains standard maps. The final 10-TU syntax
pass completed after those fixes.

The facade helper passes 29/29 normal correctness tests and 29/29 ASan/UBSan
tests with leak detection after the latest reserve/set-key-iteration
additions. The exact sources are
`reversible_cell_map.hpp` (SHA-256
`3b257cfc9d7663829eeea0b4645fb13cb02f23dfaa74c82665622b2f4a404484`) and
`reversible_cell_map_test.cpp` (SHA-256
`fd992e00b4deb3bce0ae45ebedb9b9e44ec6b2a15fc26ccdd3bf8267674f7695`). No
Vortex test binary or linked engine object has been built from this overlay,
and no full engine correctness pass is claimed.

## Remaining gates

1. Rebase after M4's OperandList API integration. M4 changes `resolveCell`'s
   first argument from vector to span and changes wing APIs; do not import M4
   changes into an M5 patch.
2. Re-run syntax with the same baseline M4 revision for every affected TU,
   then link/run targeted comparison, binding, frame, guard, stream, closure,
   resume, choice, mutation-group, and prune tests using overlay object paths.
3. Compare snapshot observable state and serialized binding output between
   standard-map and facade runs. Hash order differs, so compare logical results
   rather than bucket or iteration sequence unless a public ordering is found.
4. Recheck source ref/iterator invalidation at every modified call site after
   rebase. No VM alias promotion while any path holds an element reference
   across table mutation or relies on standard `unordered_map` iterator/swap
   stability.
5. Only after this snapshot-only overlay passes and M3/M4 are integrated should
   M5 introduce the keyed trail. At that point, replace the physical prune loop
   with trail-aware erase, keep absent keys and old shared payloads until the
   outer boundary retires, and add the outer-choice / arena-release / prune /
   rollback regression before removing snapshots.

# Isolated M5a reversible cell table design

Status: isolated implementation and GTest draft; not integrated into the repository. The current pair-backed API/hash draft compiled with Clang and passed 29 tests normally and under ASan/UBSan with leak detection. These are container-helper checks, not engine integration or performance evidence.

## Decision

Use a VM-specific keyed open-addressed table with allocator-aware nontrivial slot lifetime. Do not instantiate M3 FlatU32Map: its actual contract requires Value to be trivially copyable, while VM values include shared_ptr, optional, and payload-bearing values.

A slot has probing state Empty, Deleted, or Occupied. Occupied owns a key and an outer optional<Value>. A disengaged outer optional means retained-absent: the key remains searchable for rollback but is invisible to find, contains, iteration, size, and equality. For CellReferenceMap the nested Value may itself be optional<CellRef>, so:
- no occupied slot: logical key absent;
- occupied slot plus disengaged outer optional: logically absent but retained for undo;
- occupied slot plus engaged outer optional containing nullopt: present-unbound;
- occupied slot plus engaged outer optional containing CellRef: present-bound.

A set uses ReversibleCellSet<Key> over a unit/monostate value.

There is one physical bucket per key. With any choice or local savepoint active, logical erase moves the old Value into the already-reserved VM trail record and resets the slot outer optional while keeping its key Occupied. Inserting the same key fills that slot. Undoing that insert resets the outer optional and leaves the retained key. Undoing the earlier erase then reconstructs the old Value into the key slot. This works for repeated erase/insert/erase nesting because replay is LIFO and old values live in distinct trail records. No per-key historical lineage state is needed. A key inserted only under a live boundary also leaves a harmless retained-absent slot on undo; the final-boundary sweep reclaims it.

When no rollback boundary is active, erase may transition directly to Deleted. When the last boundary closes, sweep Occupied slots with disengaged outer optional to Deleted. Never sweep while any live choice/savepoint may restore the key.

## Expected VM value traits to verify in implementation

- CellReferenceMap value is optional<CellRef>; scalar optional moves without throwing.
- StreamMap value is shared_ptr<vector<CellRef>>; shared_ptr move is noexcept. The vector pointee is not moved during map rehash; trail retains its owning handle.
- IteratorMap value is shared_ptr<IteratorState>; handle move is noexcept. IteratorState payload changes are first-write snapshots, not map rehash copies.
- Typed sets use monostate values.
- GuardStackMap, PendingGuardMap, GuardScopeMap, and MutationGroupMap values are shared_ptr<const ...>; handle move is noexcept.
- cursorPC value is optional<CellRef>; streamCursor scalar is optional<CellRef>.
- ActivationStack value (vector<shared_ptr<const ActivationFrame>>) is noexcept movable with std::allocator, but the accepted design still uses per-frame push/pop trail inverses so it does not move whole stacks into every record.

The header statically requires nothrow move construction/destruction, but those traits alone cannot prove a user-defined noexcept move/destructor is allocation-free. Supported Value types must additionally guarantee allocation-free noexcept move/destruction semantically. The test source includes vortex_vm.hpp and statically checks actual mapped aliases for CellReferenceMap, StreamMap, IteratorMap, guard/pending/scope/group handles, and ActivationStack. Representative stream-handle and ActivationStack map undo tests arm the table PMR resource before undo; this catches table PMR allocation, not arbitrary allocations made internally by a Value move. Allocation freedom for the tested standard aliases follows from their specified representation and operations (`optional<CellRef>`, `shared_ptr` handle moves, and default-allocator vector move); do not generalize to arbitrary Value types. ActivationStack still uses per-frame push/pop inverse in production; its map test checks only its default-allocator move trait/lifetime. Do not infer ABI size or relocate with memcpy. CellRef hashing must be noexcept for lookup/undo paths.

## Rehash and operation contract

- Rehash/growth allocates and default-constructs replacement slots before moving anything from the old table. If preparation fails, old table remains logically and physically unchanged.
- After allocation succeeds, reinsert keys in their original Occupied state. Move-construct live values into replacement storage; retained-absent slots copy key/state and no value. Require noexcept move construction and destruction for VM Value types, or reject that instantiation. Never memcpy nontrivial values.
- Rehash preserves retained-absent keys so later undo finds them by key. Trail records never retain bucket pointers or indices across growth.
- Prepared capability carries owner/generation. Any intervening mutation/rehash invalidates it. It is valid only during the owning map object lifetime; callers must neither retain it past owner destruction nor use it across destruction/address reuse. No stale-handle guarantee is provided. VM secures trail vector and boundary touched-set capacity before writing an undo record, then table preparation, then publishes record/touched key, then performs nonthrowing commit. If preparation fails, staged trail record is withdrawn without allocation and logical state remains unchanged.
- Prepared insert distinguishes live from retained-absent: a live insert is duplicate; retained-absent can reuse its bucket. For a new key, grow/rehash before commit.
- Prepared erase/replacement resolves current live key by key lookup. Commit moves old Value to preconstructed trail storage without allocation. Erase under an active boundary keeps Occupied+empty; otherwise it marks Deleted. Replacement keeps the bucket live.
- Undo insertion by key destroys current live Value and leaves Occupied+empty until the entire rollback range has replayed. Undo paths never refuse merely because the uint64 generation counter saturated: preparation is disabled at max, generation saturates without wrapping, and keyed undo/reclamation still run. Undo erase by key moves its trail-owned Value into the retained slot. Undo replacement by key replaces current Value with old trail value. Undo is noexcept and allocates nothing.
- Retention policy/depth belongs to VortexVM boundaries, not global static state. Pass retain policy explicitly or via scoped internal guard. Reclaim retained keys only after final boundary retires.
- Live iteration skips Deleted and Occupied+empty. Logical size counts only Occupied+engaged. Equality compares live keys/values independent of bucket order.
- Copy semantics must distinguish logical snapshots from rollback storage. Snapshot-oracle copy should expose live entries only; a physical rollback copy with trail must preserve retained keys. Simpler option is delete adapter copying and keep snapshot oracle on current standard maps.
- Copy assignment builds complete replacement with destination allocator before swap. PMR move/copy allocator rules need deliberate noexcept claims.

## VM map API compatibility and measured slot layout

The pointer-returning `findValue(key)` is a low-level keyed undo helper, not a
replacement for production `unordered_map` aliases. The isolated facade also
drafts `find/end`, forward iteration whose dereference is an actual
`pair<const CellRef, Value>&`, range iteration, `operator[]`, `at`, `emplace`,
`insert_or_assign`, key/iterator erase, `clear`, and same-resource `swap`.
`findValue` remains explicitly named for keyed undo. Iterators expose real pair
references; they are not proxies and use no aliasing casts.

To combine standard pairs with retained absent keys, each slot has probe state,
a plain retained `CellRef`, and an optional live
`pair<const CellRef, Value>`. The retained key is consulted only in Occupied
slots, so 0 and high-bit values remain valid. Refill/undo uses
`optional::emplace(piecewise_construct, ...)`; it never assigns a pair with a
const key. A local Clang probe against actual `vortex_vm.hpp` types measured
the old `{state, optional<Key>, optional<Value>}` and proposed
`{state, Key, optional<pair<const Key, Value>>}` at identical sizes on this
target: 24 bytes for `optional<CellRef>` with 4-byte alignment, 40 bytes for
each measured shared_ptr-valued alias with 8-byte alignment, and 48 bytes for
the `ActivationStack` vector value with 8-byte alignment. This is an ABI-local
measurement, not a portable size guarantee; rerun per target ABI.

The facade matches observed source syntax, not every `unordered_map` guarantee.
Flat-table rehash invalidates entry iterators and references; standard
unordered_map preserves element references across rehash. A source audit found
current `find` results are consumed locally; stream and iterator handles are
copied into source snapshots before target writes, and the range loops in
`vortex_bindings.cpp` do not mutate the same map. Choice, binding, and frame
restore paths use staged copy/swap and do not carry entry iterators through the
swap. Standard iterators survive unordered_map swap and then refer into the
other container, while this facade's iterators retain their original owner and
are invalidated by swap. The observed restore sites do not keep an iterator
over that swap, but integration must preserve this fact. The VortexVM tables
are private members. This still needs review against
the integration diff; new code must not hold entry refs across same-map
mutation, rehash, or staged swap. Copy optional/shared_ptr values before writes.

`pruneAssemblyState()` currently uses `std::erase_if` over reversible tables.
The draft supplies its own `eraseIf` helper and adds no `std` overload. `clear`
and basic `eraseIf` are irreversible and valid only when no boundary can undo
those entries. VM prune with surviving boundaries
needs a trail-aware loop: stage each keyed erase record before mutation, retain
the absent physical slot through the outer boundary, and keep old shared
payloads alive for rollback. The draft `eraseIf` is not suitable for that path.

Observed map forms to preserve at integration are `find/end/it->first/it->second`,
live range structured bindings, `contains/size/empty`, `operator[]`, `at`,
`emplace`, `insert_or_assign`, `erase(key/iterator)`, `clear`, and staged
`swap`. `clear`, key/iterator erase, and `eraseIf` are irreversible and require
boundary-free use. Reversible deletion only uses `prepareErase` plus
`commitErase` with caller-owned optional trail storage; convenience erase has
no retention flag, so it cannot retain a key while dropping its old payload.
The typed set draft exposes `insert(key)` as a bool plus
`contains/erase/size/swap` for the observed ignored-result call sites; it does
not claim the full unordered_set iterator API. Staged `swap` requires the
same PMR resource; current Vortex aliases use the default allocator, but an
integrated allocator policy must preserve staged restore paths. Audit snapshot copies
separately: ChoicePoint, RuntimeBindingSnapshot, SavedBindings, and staged
frame maps use ordinary unordered_map storage; their copy semantics must stay
logical/live-only. Keep non-reversible tables such as opcodeMap_, cursorPC_,
resume maps, frame-local backing maps, and memoized opcode maps outside this
adapter unless the plan explicitly adds them.

The default isolated `CellRefHash` reuses M3's SplitMix64-style avalanche
arithmetic (golden-ratio add, xor shifts 30/27/31, the two established 64-bit
mix multipliers). This avoids identity-hash clustering when op indices have
power-of-two stride and the table masks to power-of-two capacity. The targeted
8,192-bucket/4,096-stride-key probe has max linear-probe length below 64; a
constant-hash map test still checks collision correctness. This is a small
distribution sanity check, not a throughput benchmark. Avoid duplicating this
mixer in the final integration: extract/reuse the planned tiny engine-private
CellRef/u32 hasher with the M3 owner, not a generic library facility.

## Scope and open questions

This is container-only: no trail, ChoicePoint edits, production wiring, or benchmark. It is not a complete M5a implementation. Keep current ChoicePoint snapshots in production during M5a. Before rollback is enabled, settle:
1. Normal insert/erase/assign versus explicit prepare/commit API.
2. Trail staging: reserve vmTrail_ first and hold an uncommitted local entry; prepare table, then nonthrowingly publish record and perform commit. Avoid commit-before-record.
3. Copy semantics for live snapshots versus retained tombstones. Could expose logicalCopy(resource); simpler alternative is delete physical copy and keep oracle on std::unordered_map.
4. Whether each table uses per-instance std::pmr::memory_resource for deterministic failure injection.
5. Static noexcept traits and actual ABI sizes for every Value. The isolated code constrains map Value move/destruction and Hash construction/invocation; integration must still assert every instantiated VM alias. shared_ptr, optional<CellRef>, and monostate are straightforward; ActivationStack needs per-frame push/pop inverse, not whole-stack Value.

## Failure injection

Use a per-instance PMR memory_resource that throws on selected allocation ordinal. It must be attached to the table and, in integrated work, VM trail/touched storage, not process-global. For this adapter draft, fail each table allocation ordinal (initial allocation, replacement allocation) and assert unchanged logical contents, retained keys and retry. No build, runtime, or timing evidence is claimed.


## Boundary-aware arena pruning

The VM's arena-driven prune is a logical mutation when rollback boundaries survive. `AssemblyTransaction` releases its mark before pruning; `SolutionDriver` cuts only to its saved base depth, then releases and prunes; `CompileArea` releases the query mark and prunes after the driver. The base VM choice depth may therefore remain nonzero.

Under strict arena mark LIFO, a surviving ChoicePoint snapshot cannot contain a cell key born inside the just-released region: the choice predates the region and that key did not exist at its snapshot. However, its trail can contain writes made later to those keys. `pruneAssemblyState` must logically erase through the reversible table, retaining absent slots and trail payloads until full rollback; unwind may temporarily restore dead ids, but may not dereference them before earlier records reach the absent baseline. `streamCursor` follows the same rule. Resume control maps remain untrailed; erasures from cellReferences during resume pruning do not. A dedicated VM regression must cover outer choice + post-mark stream/reference keys + release/prune + rollback, including streamCursor and shared payload lifetime. This is not a reason to forbid nested SolutionDriver or require zero choice depth.

Generation policy in the header draft saturates rather than wraps: no new prepared token is issued at max; growth preflights two remaining increments (rehash plus commit) before physical allocation; commit only accepts tokens created below max; rollback and retained-key cleanup still proceed at max. Multi-entry visitors are invoked as stable lvalues. This protects no-throw undo from epoch exhaustion.

The executable-style GTest source is `reversible_cell_map_test.cpp`; `reversible_cell_map_test_draft.md` keeps the broader reference-model and future VM-level test matrix. The suite before the R2 source-only additions checked map/set semantics, initial/growth allocation refusal and retry, copy/move failure atomicity, retained-key rehash and refilling, nested same-key undo, no-allocation commit/undo, shared-value lifetime, copy/move token invalidation, and logical-copy visibility. New but not yet run cases instantiate actual VM mapped aliases and test representative PMR-allocation-disabled undo.

# Static M5a VM map compatibility and migration plan

This is a static integration guide for the isolated pair-backed reversible map in this directory. It makes no production edits and is not evidence that the VM is ready to switch aliases. The helper is still not wired to VM trail/savepoint behavior.

## Gate before alias replacement

1. Keep existing ChoicePoint full-map snapshots as the rollback oracle. Do not retire them while M5a introduces the keyed trail.
2. Use the isolated map facade only after the independent facade review is accepted. Its observed API surface has real `pair<const CellRef, Value>` iterator references, but the vector-backed container invalidates entry references on growth and iterators on growth/swap. Current `VortexVM` table members are private and have no public getters, but source call sites must still avoid retaining element references through same-map growth or map swap. Copy mapped optional/shared_ptr handles to locals before any writes.
3. All trailable writes must be converted to prepare/publish/commit operations. Do not rely on source-compatible `operator[]`, `insert_or_assign`, `erase`, `clear`, or `eraseIf` to make a transaction. Those facade APIs are ordinary irreversible map operations. Reversible erase is only `prepareErase` then `commitErase` into caller-owned trail storage with `retainForUndo=true`; the helper intentionally exposes no convenience erase retention flag.
4. Reserve trail and boundary-touched capacity before writing a record. Rehash/table allocation must happen before record publication; after record publication only nonthrowing moves/resets and key lookup may remain. Undo/reclaim cannot allocate and cannot dereference arena cells.
5. Do not add a `std::erase_if` overload. Replace VM `std::erase_if` calls on reversible maps with an explicit trail-aware prune loop. Keep the helper's basic `eraseIf` for boundary-free cleanup only.
6. Ordinary snapshots need a separate live-only copy. `logicalCopy(resource)` copies live entries only; physical copy intentionally preserves retained tombstones for independent rollback. Preserve the snapshot oracle's current value semantics and test map state, not its bucket layout.

## Alias-by-alias action table

| VM member | Concrete value / set contents | Mutations to route | Special undo contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

`opcodeMap_`, `memoizedOps_`, `cursorPC_`, `resumeValues_`, `resumeTokenIds_`, frame-local maps, descriptor maps, and `next*Id_` counters are not ordinary choice-trail aliases. `cursorPC_` is restored by relevant local savepoints only. Resume maps/IDs remain untrailed control state; any `cellReferences_` entry they remove still follows regular register undo. `opcodeMap_` may be physically pruned after arena release.

## Route conversion inventory

### `vortex_vm.cpp`

- `writeCellReferences` (713-739): central scalar write funnel. Convert presence/value mutation to keyed insert/replace/erase trail records; preserve present-unbound entries and typed-register exclusion.
- `clearTypedRegister` (`vortex_streams.cpp:33-38`): central register cleanup candidate, but must stage all four tables (two membership sets, stream/iterator payloads) and optional scalar reference as one coherent register change.
- `setCursorOpcode` (623-654), `pruneCursors` (688), `pruneAssemblyState` (544-560): bulk key removal. Cleanup must use explicit trail records when a choice/local savepoint survives. `pruneAssemblyState` also updates streamCursor and calls `pruneResumeState`.
- `trimGuardScopes` (453-466), `removeValidatedGuardObligations` (427-451), `abortOwnedMutationGroups` (468-509), guard/mutation-scope execution (1922+, 2142+), mutation-group completion/abort (2353-2442), and `driveGuardValidation` (2446+): currently copy/mutate/swap one or more maps. Keep this staged code as oracle until each full call transaction has local-savepoint coverage. Do not translate only the final map write if multi-table/callback effects can fail earlier.
- `abortOwnedMutationGroups` and `abortScopedChoices` (1548-1579): noexcept cut/rollback-like routes. Trail must unwind before arena release; rollback stays allocation-free. Preserve no-cut-callback behavior for scoped abort.
- `backtrack` (1436-1490): unwind VM trail to ChoicePoint mark before releasing ArenaManifold mark; then route PC/stackFrame and preserve cross-cursor/mutation barriers.
- `cut` (1493-1546): discard boundaries without undo, but retain child committed trail entries while any outer boundary exists. Reclaim trail/tombstones only after final boundary retires.
- `stealNearRootChoicePoint` (1604-1623): rebase surviving trail watermarks/prefix and promptly release dead payloads. OR-parallel shadow prefixes are serialized state, never trail pointers.

### `vortex_streams.cpp`

- `requireStreamCursor` (40-66): whole-table clear only when contract proves no surviving rollback boundary; otherwise it must trail each old stream/iterator handle and membership plus scalar cursor.
- `executeCellRefCopy` (98+), `StreamClear`, `StreamAppend`, `StreamBegin`/`StreamReverseBegin`, `RankBegin`, `IteratorNext`, `PinHistorical`, and stream concatenation: source snapshots already precede target writes in copy routes. Preserve that ordering; trail target state before any payload mutation. IteratorNext must snapshot before `.unique()` and interior updates, then ensure output/arena-write refusal cannot leave the advance committed.
- Other clear/erase sites (35-38, 191-195, 262-298, 332-336, 399-410, 495-499): convert every coupled set/ref/payload mutation, not just map payload.

### `vortex_frames.cpp`, closures, bindings, contracts, resume, comparison

- `invokeFramePrepared` (338-500): currently full copies refs/streams/iterators/sets/activation frames and cursor fields around an arena mark, catch swaps them back. This is one named local snapshot path. Introduce a VMSavepoint covering all VM writes before alias migration; trail unwind must happen before release.
- Frame close/cleanup (around 655-707): stream/ref/payload/set and activation-stack erases must be atomic; keep old shared handles and stack capacity.
- `executeClosure` and closure-create paths (`vortex_closures.cpp`): route output and frame setup mutations through the same local transaction; preserve alias-freeze and failed-create retry behavior.
- `vortex_bindings.cpp`: snapshot restore and comparison traversal use range structured bindings and `find/end/second`. The syntax is covered by the facade, but do not carry element refs through same-map mutation; snapshot old handles first.
- `prepareTypeContract` / `executeTypeContract` (`vortex_contracts.cpp:31+`, VM 4814-4850): present-unbound reset, erase, and emplace are distinct states and must keep output slots coherent.
- `executeResumeInit` (`vortex_resume.cpp:30-108`): output cell reference is trailed; resume control values/IDs remain deliberately untrailed; failure cleanup must preserve monotonic token ID and current failed-init behavior.
- `comparisonOperand` (`vortex_comparison.cpp:24-45`) consumes concrete CellReferenceMap and map/set APIs read-only; adapt signature or alias while preserving comparison semantics and VQL budget behavior.

## Snapshot oracle and transition order

Keep `ChoicePoint` copies of the ten state maps/sets and `streamCursor_` as the differential oracle while the trail is introduced. Four local whole-map transaction paths identified in the mutation inventory (frame invoke, restore-bindings, guard validation, mutation-scope/group staged transactions) need explicit VMSavepoints before any snapshot is retired. On operation failure, reverse VM trail first, then release/rollback arena mark; restore local-only `cursorPC_`, counters, route metadata, and scalar cursors with current semantics. For restore-bindings, preserve failure restoration of counters, streamCursor and cursorPC. A failed multi-table mutation must not leave a typed membership without its payload or scalar reference.

At choice push, snapshot/trail watermark records must be secured before publishing the mark. At nested commit/cut, inner touched-key state may retire, but outer records remain. At rollback, reverse replay by key may temporarily move dead `CellRef` values into tables after `pruneAssemblyState`; it may only move/destroy handles and must not consult ArenaManifold until replay reaches absent baseline. At root steal, rebase the trail to the surviving boundary before dropping old snapshots; validate exact prefix accounting and destructed shared payload watermarks.

## Required regression gates before VM alias migration

1. Existing Vortex VM suites unchanged against snapshot oracle; add a test-only differential checker comparing all ten maps/sets, cursorPC for local savepoints, streamCursor, arena state, cycle/fuel, resume invariants, Dewey/spark metadata and callback events.
2. Key state matrix: missing vs present-unbound vs present-bound; high-bit and zero keys; erase/reinsert/replace same key under nested boundaries; rehash between erase and undo; shared payload lifetime until restore/drop.
3. Allocation failpoints at trail reserve, touched-key reserve, table initial allocation/growth, payload copy, stack growth and local savepoint creation. Before commit, logical maps and arena remain unchanged. Undo/cut/reclaim remain allocation-free.
4. Outer choice + post-choice stream/iterator/reference keys + inner arena release + `pruneAssemblyState` + outer rollback, including streamCursor and shared payload lifetime. Include resume-token pruning and local-savepoint path if supported.
5. Differential route coverage: backtrack, cut, scoped abort, mutation-group abort, guard validation retry, closure failure/retry, restore-bindings failure, frame invoke failure, ResumeInit failure, and root-steal rebase. Ensure undo never dereferences a pruned arena cell.
6. Comparison adapter compile/use coverage (`vql_comparison_vm_test.cpp`) and separate logical snapshot-copy assertions.

Do not enable performance tuning or retire map snapshots until this correctness/failure matrix passes. The helper's 27 normal and ASan/UBSan tests validate only its standalone container contracts; they do not satisfy these VM integration gates.

# M5a ReversibleCellMap test draft

The executable test source is reversible_cell_map_test.cpp. This file records the broader matrix; all failure injection uses a per-instance PMR resource, never global mutable fail state.

## Logical state and lifetime

- Missing key differs from present-unbound and present-bound for Value = optional<CellRef>.
- Retained-absent is invisible to find, contains, iteration, size and equality.
- Erased shared_ptr/vector/optional payloads are destroyed exactly once after trail ownership ends; no bytewise copying.
- ReversibleCellSet exposes only live membership and undoes erase without allocation.

## Nested reference-model cases

1. Insert K under boundary A; undo insertion; K absent. Reclaim retained key only after A closes and its rollback replay is complete.
2. Start K=A; boundary A; erase K (record owns A); insert K=B into retained slot; boundary B; erase K (record owns B); insert K=C. Undo B insert gives absent; undo B erase gives K=B; undo A insert gives absent; undo A erase gives K=A. Assert one physical bucket for K through test-only diagnostic inspection.
3. Start K=A; boundary A replace K=B; boundary B replace K=C; undo B restores B, undo A restores A.
4. Start K=A; boundary A erase; insert K=B; undo insert gives absent; undo erase gives A.
5. Start absent K; boundary A insert K=B; boundary B erase; undo B gives B; undo A gives absent.
6. Use shared_ptr and nontrivial values; verify trail-held old versions survive exactly through their watermark and are destroyed promptly at commit/steal/rollback retirement.
7. Nested commit retains child undo records for outer rollback but drops child touched-key bookkeeping. Child rollback restores its entry state.

## Rehash and no-allocation restore

- Force growth with live, Deleted, and retained-absent slots; verify key-based undo after rehash.
- Rehash between erase and rollback, then undo by key; trail cannot retain bucket pointer/index.
- Exercise erase, same-key insert, growth, undo insert, undo erase.
- After setup, reject every subsequent allocation and run undo insert/erase/replace and final tombstone sweep; all complete.
- Fail each table allocation (initial slots, replacement slots, copy/logicalCopy). Old logical map stays equal and retry succeeds.
- Copy/move with retained slots: explicitly test physical-copy policy; logicalCopy includes live entries only.
- Stale preparation after mutation/rehash refuses commit without corrupting counts.
- Capacity overflow returns named failure and publishes no mutation.

## Property/reference model

Generate deterministic sequences on small keys/values: insert, replace, erase, begin boundary, commit, rollback, rehash. std::unordered_map snapshot stack is oracle. After each step compare live lookup, key/value iteration as sets, size and logical equality. Include repeated reuse of one key and nested boundary sequences; ignore physical iteration order.

## Eventual VM-level coverage not proved by this adapter

The adapter does not prove VMTrailEntry lifetime, touched-set ownership, stream/iterator first-write coalescing, cursorPC local savepoints, resume behavior, arena ordering, cut callbacks, mutation-group abort, or root-steal rebase. Keep the regression requirements in /tmp/perf-m5-mutator-inventory.md.

# M3 C2 lookup memory accounting

Collected 2026-11-16 from the current frozen C2 headers and
`tools/lookup_memory_probe.cpp`. This is allocation/capacity accounting only;
it contains no throughput or latency measurement.

## Method

- Built the standalone probe and a small `sizeof`/`alignof` harness with the
  Makefile-probed control compiler (`/usr/bin/clang++`, Clang 23.1.4),
  `PERF_MODE=control`, and the flags captured by `make -s
  PERF_MODE=control perf-print-flags`. No PGO flags or engine objects were
  used. The exact control CXXFLAGS are recorded in `abi.json`.
- Ran the probe serially with requested sizes 10,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000.
  Raw CSV output is in `count-10000.csv`, `count-100000.csv`, and
  `count-1000000.csv`.
- The probe reports current and peak bytes requested through its PMR resource.
  Its own pointer ledger uses the default allocator, outside that resource.
  `std::unordered_map` columns are allocation controls measured through the
  same counting resource; reserved controls call `reserve(live_count)` first.
  These are allocator-requested bytes/capacities, not process RSS or complete
  object footprint. Timing was not collected.
- In `byRef` rows, the CSV field named
  `overflow_or_mapped_value_bytes` is actually the `FlatU32Map` bucket
  capacity (a slot count), not a byte count. In `births-prepared` rows the
  corresponding field is the mapped-value size in bytes. The PMR
  `current_bytes` and `peak_bytes` fields are byte counts for both.

## C2 known-short versus an intentionally inflated known hint

Both rows below are current C2 measurements with different *provided known*
hints. The three-entry fixture uses keys 1, 5,000, and 9,999. With its known
path count of 148, `byRef` has dense capacity 64 values plus 8 presence bytes;
its sparse overflow has bucket capacity 8. At the measured 48-byte pair size
plus one presence bit per bucket, that overflow contributes 66 bytes. The
measured current and peak PMR bytes are both 330 (256 value bytes + 8
presence bytes + 66 overflow bytes). Birth-map current/peak is 272 bytes. The
same fixture with an intentionally inflated known 10,000-op hint produces
`byRef` dense capacity 10,000, 1,250
presence bytes, no overflow allocation, current 41,250 bytes, and peak 61,875
bytes. Birth-map bytes are unchanged at 272.

The 10,000-op-hint row is an accounting proxy for an inflated known hint; it
is not the unknown-hint fallback (which uses 4,096) and is not a historical C1
production measurement. Both fixture rows repeat identically in all three
requested-size runs because the fixture remains three entries and varies only
its hint. They demonstrate capacity effects, not a speed benefit.

## ABI sizes

The standalone C2 header harness reports `Manifold` 488 bytes (alignment 8),
`ManifoldOpIndexMap` 216 bytes (alignment 8), and
`StructureBirthInfo` 40 bytes (alignment 8). A
`pair<const uint32_t, StructureBirthInfo>` is 48 bytes. The `std::unordered_map`
and `std::pmr::unordered_map` container headers are 56 and 64 bytes,
respectively. These header/object sizes are separate from dynamic PMR bytes and
are not shared-memory totals.

The archived comparison artifact
[m3-abi-accounting.json](/data/git/gleditor-restore/build/performance/comparisons/m3-abi-accounting.json)
has SHA-256
`59837afb4354a78c09fd8624344858962b5bdfe8a9a35480bc3fa74245dae58e`.
It records P3 at 296 bytes and the prior C hybrid-unordered variant at 544
bytes. Against those archived measurements, current C2 at 488 bytes is +192
bytes versus P3 and 56 bytes below prior C. These comparisons use the
artifact's recorded compiler/stdlib/flags and are header-size differences
only. The full current C2 source hashes, compiler target, standard library,
and build flags are in `abi.json`.
